title: GemmaJury — self docket

models.orchestration: Sequential ingest -> Parallel Gemma panel -> Gemini verdict

strengths: ADK SequentialAgent + ParallelAgent is the control plane.
Gemma 4 is the three specialist judges; Gemini only stewards.
Tools hit live public GitHub and demo URLs.
code.opinion: This is a real multi-agent workflow. Gemma is the panel, not a sticker.

strengths: Scorecard UI makes the three-judge loop visible.
Sample docket keeps the demo alive without keys.
risks: A hosted Cloud Run URL must stay on the Devpost form.
demo.opinion: The product is the verdict page. Show ingest, three Gemma cards, then the opinion.

strengths: Judging submissions is a chore that needs specialists.
Gemma as jury and Gemini as clerk is the right story for this contest.
risks: Meta-projects can feel cute if the rubrics stay vague.
creativity.opinion: A single LLM call cannot honestly judge code, a demo reel, and taste at once. The panel earns its keep.

synthesis: GemmaJury turns hackathon judging into an autonomous workflow: Gemini 3.5 builds the docket, three Gemma 4 judges score in parallel, and a steward writes a weighted opinion a human can read aloud.
next_actions: Deploy the UI to Cloud Run and paste the public URL on Devpost.
Record the demo against a third-party public repo.
Quote exact README lines as citations.
evidence_excerpt: Recorded self-verdict used when DEMO_MODE is on or no API key is present.
